active_themes.label: Warsh Takes Office
active_themes.summary: Warsh's confirmation removed all uncertainty about rate cuts; the market's focus has shifted entirely to whether cuts land into a weakening consumer and sticky $90+ oil. Today's mixed market action (Nasdaq relief vs. Dow weakness) reflects the split thesis: tech believes AI upside offsets macro headwinds; broad market is skeptical. The deciding factor is May 29 consumer spending data—if spending shows weakness, lenders' early tightening will be validated, and Warsh's cuts arrive into a self-reinforcing demand destruction loop.

active_themes.label: Oil Holds $90 Floor
active_themes.summary: $90+ oil confirmed as structural after three consecutive days above $88. Today brought fresh Iran escalation risk (attack on UAE nuclear plant condemned by UN Security Council, Israeli ground operations expanding in Lebanon, tanker explosion off Oman) but oil did not spike materially—suggesting the market is already pricing this risk. The next signal is $95+ for three consecutive days, which would confirm a regime shift higher rather than a range bounce. Until that trigger, oil is holding its floor but not breaking out on headlines alone.

active_themes.label: Lenders Front-Running Cuts
active_themes.summary: The incentive structure for early credit withdrawal is now clear to all institutional lenders: Warsh's cuts are coming, yield compression is inevitable, and depositors will flee to money markets. No major lender announcement today, but this silence is itself the signal—banks are quietly tightening before competing on yield rates intensifies. The mechanism is locked in. What matters now is whether May 29 spending data validates their pessimism (spending weak → lenders were right to pull early → equities capitulate) or proves them premature (spending holds → over-tightening was unnecessary → credit reverses and equities rally).

active_themes.label: Credit Withdrawal Waiting on Data
active_themes.summary: Lenders are rationally front-running but have not yet announced material tightening publicly. The mechanism is invisible until May 29, when consumer spending data will reveal whether credit destruction is already underway. Today's divergence (Nasdaq +1.19% vs. Dow -0.23%) reflects the market's uncertainty: tech believes consumers are resilient; broad indices are pricing in credit-driven weakness. This is the highest-stakes data point on the calendar for the next 72 hours.

active_themes.label: Long Duration Repricing Locked In
active_themes.summary: The 30-year yield is at 2007 highs; institutional consensus is already priced that Warsh's cuts weaken the dollar, push oil higher, and force long-duration repricing as inflation expectations reset. No new development today, but today's mixed equity action confirms the consensus is holding: the bond market and the broad equity market agree that cuts into $90+ oil and tightening credit is a negative trade-off, not a healing scenario. Today's Nasdaq relief on AI is a tactical relief, not a reframe of that structural view.
